4: Unit 2 starts with how a group reaches the engine.
An Entra group reaches Sequel Server as a group login, then a database user added to a role.
The data platform book's Chapter 16, Groups, Roles and How Membership Reaches the Engine, makes one rule central.
Each Entra group grants exactly one role, on one database, in one environment, so the group's name says what it grants.
The model stays flat, because dynamic groups can't contain groups, and nesting builds on behavior that is unsupported, ending or undocumented.
Members are listed directly, by rule or by assignment.
One group, one role is checked where the roles are known: the login plan from Module 4 warns.
The group map carries grants per instance, not roles per database, so it doesn't repeat the check.
5: Each legacy group then lands in one of four patterns.
Pattern one: organization-derived groups, kept from the org chart, become dynamic.
The kit writes the rule on the H R organization code in extension attribute ten, with clauses that require an enabled account and a member, not a guest.
Never on department or job title.

Pattern two: explicit role groups become assigned, managed by a delegated administrator, and eligible through pim when the group holds sys-admin or security admin. Pattern three: distribution lists become mail-only.
Update the Sequel Server Agent operator's address, and give it no login.
Pattern four: mail-enabled security groups split in two, a mail-only group and an assigned security group, with the pairing recorded in both descriptions.
And when a group's codes aren't recorded, the target says to ask H R for the code before writing the rule.
6: Unit 3 is the attribute, pim and the perimeter.
Under dynamic membership, whoever can write the attribute a rule reads controls access.
So the book's Chapter 17 has rules read H R owned codes, such as the organization code in extension attribute ten, never display strings such as department.
And every access rule excludes disabled accounts and guests.
Groups that hold sys-admin are never dynamic.
Microsoft Learn says pim for Groups doesn't work on dynamic groups, or on groups synchronized from on premises.
So privileged groups are cloud-only and assigned.
Otherwise, whoever can write the attribute could make someone sys-admin. Conditional Access then sits in front of every user token.
But it applies to users, not to managed identities, so applications are covered by the application chain in Chapter 7, not by Conditional Access.
